en: The Twelve-Verse Praise to Ādibuddha: Om, homage to Ādibuddha!
Homage to you who are the form of the Buddha; homage to you who are the form of the Dharma.
Salutations to you who are the form of the Saṃgha; salutations to the essence of the five Buddhas. || 1 ||
Salutations to you who are the form of earth; salutations to you who are the form of water; salutations to you who are the form of fire;
salutations to you who are the form of wind; salutations to you who are the form of space. || 2 ||
Salutations to you, who are Brahmā in the form of *sattva*, Viṣṇu in the form of *rajas*, Maheśa in the form of *tamas*, and the embodiment of knowledge.
Homage to you whose nature is wisdom and skillful means, to you whose form is secret; homage to you whose form is the world-protectors of the directions, to you whose form is the universe. || 4 ||
Homage to the eye and form, to the ear, to the nose and form, to the tongue, to the body and form, and to the mind in the form of the glorious Dharma. || 5 ||
Salutations to you who are the form of form; salutations to you whose form is taste.
Salutations to you whose forms are fragrance, sound, and touch. 6.
Homage to the one who assumes the form of the Dharma, whose nature is the six sense-faculties;
homage to the one whose form is the aggregate of flesh, bone, fat, and marrow. || 7 ||
Salutations to you whose form is the beauty of all moving beings and whose embodiment is the stability of all unmoving things;
salutations to you whose form is the delusion of animals and whose form is the source of all wonders.
Salutations again and again to You, the creator of the universe; to You who are birth, death in the form of time, the future, the aged, and the child.
Salutations to the one whose form consists of prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna;
salutations to the enjoyer whose form is both colored and colorless, and who is the source of those [vital breaths]. 10.
To the Sun, who is the form of day; to the Moon, whose form is night;
to Him who is the form of the lunar days (tithis), and whose body consists of the constellations, yogas, days of the week, and so forth.
Homage again and again to you who possess both external and internal forms, to the worldly one; homage to you who are Nirvāṇa, and homage to you of manifold forms.
If a person, firm in constant resolve, recites the twelve [verses] of the *Ādibuddha* in the morning, they will surely obtain whatever they desire. (13)
The *Śrīmañjuśrīkṛtamādibuddhadvādaśakastotra* is completed.
